newsitem.title: MEXICO: FBI investigates death of Mexico journalist.
newsitem.headline: FBI investigates death of Mexico journalist.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is helping Mexico probe the murder this week of a crusading anti-narcotics journalist gunned down in a remote U.S.-Mexico border town, an FBI agent said on Friday.

Benjamin Flores Gonzalez, 29, died on Tuesday in a hail of bullets outside the office of the newspaper he directed in the desert town of San Luis Rio Colorado, on the Arizona border in Mexico's northern Sonora state.
Mexican judicial authorities and fellow journalists said Flores' death may be connected to his investigative reports on the drug trade.
FBI special agent Jack Callahan, based in Phoenix, Arizona, told Reuters that U.S. investigators were working on the case.
"We're assisting the Mexican authorities," he said, but declined to comment on what role the FBI was playing.

Mexico's Reforma daily said Sonora's state attorney had requested the FBI's collaboration, and said the U.S. agency had information on who owned the murderers' getaway car, which had California license plates.
Flores, who founded La Prensa daily five years ago, was ambushed by four men in a gray sedan who pumped him full of bullets from an AK-47 rifle and a .22 calibre pistol.
Bullets ricocheted off the walls and bystanders said they found about 30 cartridge cases on the blood-drenched footpath.
Police said the victim had been facing five lawsuits for defamation because of his investigative stories.

La Prensa's news editor, Jesus Barraza, said Flores also had received a death threat from a lieutenant of dead drug lord Amado Carrillo Fuentes, who died in mysterious circumstances two weeks ago after extensive plastic surgery.
International journalists' groups have urged Mexican authorities to give the case top priority.

The Inter-American Press Society has pressed Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo to conduct a rapid investigation, and France's Reporters without Borders has also written to Zedillo requesting him to help bring the murderers to justice.

The New York-based Committee to Protect Journalists on Wednesday asked Sonora state governor Manlio Fabio Beltrones to examine whether there were any connections between Flores' death and the court cases overhanging him.

Flores, who founded La Prensa five years ago, wrote a hard-hitting column called "No Confirmada" (Unconfirmed) in which he criticised politicians, including the governor's brother Orestes Beltrones, and denounced regional drug barons, including Hector Palma, the now-jailed head of the Sinaloa cartel.
In May this year he reported the theft of half a tonne of cocaine from Federal Judicial Police Headquarters in San Luis Rio Colorado after it was confiscated by local authorities.
Police said he spent several months in jail some years ago after losing a court case against the Sonora government.
